senses.gloss:
शुशुक्वन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shining excessively,
very brilliant.

शुशुक्वनि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. resplendent, shining,
(Sāy. = दीपन-शील, Ṛg-veda VIII. 23, 5.)

शुशुक्वस्, वान्, m., Ved. one who has purified or
brightened, an illuminator, (Sāy. = शोचयिता, सर्-
वस्य प्रकाशयिता.)
शुशुक्वस् शुशुक्वस्. See under rt. 3. शुच्.

शुशुचान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shining, bright, bril-
liant, (Sāy. = दीप्यमान.)
शुशुक्षणि शुशुक्षणि in आ-शुशुक्षणि, q. v.
शुशुमा शुशुमा, f., N. of the wife of Śukra.

शुशुलूकयातु शुशुलूक-यातु, उस्, m., Ved. a
demon in the shape of an owlet, (according to Sāy.
[]
on Ṛg-veda VII. 104, 22. शुशूलूक = शिशूलूक,
a small owl; cf. उलूक-यातु.)
शुश्रुवस् शुश्रुवस्. See under rt. 1. श्रु.
शुश्रुवस्, आन्, उषी, अत्, one who has heard, &c.

शुश्रू शुश्रू, ऊस्, f. (fr. Desid. of rt. 1. श्रु),
‘one who waits on a child,’ a mother.

शुश्रूषक, अस्, आ, अम्, desirous of hearing,
attentive, obedient, attending or waiting on; (अस्),
m. an attendant, servant (comprehending five de-
scriptions of persons, viz. a pupil, a religious pupil, a
hired servant, an officer, and a slave).

शुश्रूषण, अम्, n. obedience; dutiful homage,
close and assiduous attendance, service, serving.

शुश्रूषा, f. desire or wish to hear, desire to
obey, obedience; service (said to be of five kinds,
see शुश्रूषक); obsequiousness, reverence; say-
ing, speaking, telling.
—शुश्रूषा-पर, अस्, आ, अम्,
diligent or attentive in service.

शुश्रूषित्वा, ind. having attended or waited upon
(as a slave upon his master, Manu XI. 110).

शुश्रूषु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of hearing or obey-
ing, obedient, attentive, serving, attending.

शुष् शुष् (thought to be for सुष्, which
again was probably for an original सुस्),
cl. 4. P. शुष्यति (ep. also A. -ते), शुशोष, शोक्ष्-
यति, अशुषत्, शोष्टुम्, to dry, become dry, dry
up; to wither, become withered; to languish, be-
come emaciated; to be afflicted: Caus. शोषयति,
-ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अशूशुषत्, to make dry, dry up,
wither, parch; to emaciate; to destroy; to extinguish:
Desid. शुशुक्षति: Intens. शोशुष्यते, शोशोष्टि;
[cf. Zend hushka: Gr. σαυαρός, σαυσαρισμός,
σαυκός (= शुष्क), σαυχμός, αὐχμός, σαχνός,
αὔω, αὖος, αὐστηρός: Lat. siccus: Goth. siuk,
sauht: Old Germ. siuh, siuchi, siuhjan, suht:
Angl. Sax. seoc, seac, sioc, sic, suht: Slav. such,
‘dry:’ Lith. sausa-s: Hib. seacadh, ‘parched,
frozen;’ sioc, ‘frost;’ sican.]

शूष् शूष् (also written सूष्), cl. 1. P.
शूषति, शुशूष, शूषितुम्, to bring
forth; to beget, propagate.

सूष् सूष् (= rt. शूष्, q. v.), cl. 1. P. सू-
षति, &c., to bring forth, bear; to beget.

शुष, अस्, ई, m. f. drying, drying up; a hole in
the ground.

शूष शूष, अम्, n. (perhaps connected
with rt. श्वि), Ved. strength, (according to Naigh. II.
9, Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 154, 3 = बल; cf. शुष्म;
in Naigh. III. 6 = सुख); (अस्), m., N. of a pre-
ceptor.
सूषा, f., Ved. = सूषणा above.

शुषत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. drying up, absorbing
(moisture).

शुषि, इस्, f. drying; a hole, chasm; the hollow
or groove in the fang of a snake; [cf. Gr. κυσό-ς,
κυσ-θό-ς; Lat. cun-nu-s; Lith. kuszy-s.]

शुषिर, अस्, आ, अम्, full of holes or crevices
(caused by drying), perforated, bored, pierced, full
of interstices or spaces; (अम्), n. a hole, vacuity,
chasm; the atmosphere; a wind-instrument; (अस्),
m. fire; a rat, mouse; (आ), f. a river; a sort of per-
fume (commonly called Nalī).

सुषिर, अस्, आ, अम्, (for शुषिर, q. v.), full of
holes, perforated, hollow, &c.; having spaces; slow
in articulation, = विलम्बित; (आ), f., Ved. an abyss;
(अम्), n. a hole, cavity.
शुषिल, अस्, m. ‘the dryer,’ air, wind.

शुष्क, अस्, आ, अम्, dried, dried up, dry; shriveled,
withered, emaciated, shrunk up; groundless, cause-
less; unproductive, fruitless, unprofitable; offensive;
(अम्), n., Ved. anything dry, dry wood (for lighting
fire by attrition).
—शुष्क-कलह, अस्, m. vain or
useless wrangling, a quarrel about trifles.
—शुष्क-
ता, f. or शुष्क-त्व, अम्, n. dryness.
—शुष्क-
पत्त्र, अम्, n. a dry or withered leaf; a dried pot-
herb.
—शुष्क-पर्ण, अम्, n. a dry or withered
leaf.
—शुष्क-फल, अम्, n. dry fruit.
—शुष्क-
मत्स्य, अस्, m. a dried fish.
—शुष्क-मांस,
अम्, n. dry flesh, dry meat.
—शुष्क-रेवती, f.
epithet of a particular Mātrikā or goddess presiding
over a kind of disease; [cf. रेवती, पूतना.]
—शुष्क-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, dried up.
—शुष्क-
वृक्ष, अस्, m. a dry tree; a particular plant or
shrub (= धव).
—शुष्क-वैर, अम्, n. ground-
less enmity.
—शुष्क-व्रण, अस्, m. a dried up
wound, cicatrized sore, scar.
—शुष्क-स्रोत, अस्, आ,
अम्, having the stream dried up.
—शुष्काङ्ग (˚क-
अङ्˚), अस्, ई, अम्, having shriveled limbs, emaciated,
withered; (अस्), m. a particular plant or shrub, =
धव; (ई), f. a lizard, chameleon.
—शुष्कान्न
(˚क-अन्˚), अम्, n. ‘dry food,’ rice in the husk.
—शुष्कार्द्र (˚क-आर्˚), अम्, n. dry ginger.

शुष्कल, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, m. f. n. dry flesh;
flesh; one who eats flesh.

शुष्ण, अस्, m. the sun; fire; N. of a demon of
[]
drought (represented in the Ṛg-veda as being over-
come by Indra); (अम्), n., Ved. strength, (enume-
rated among the बल-नामानि in Naigh. II. 9.)
—शुष्ण-हत्य, अम्, n., Ved. the slaughter of
Śuṣṇa.
सुष्म सुष्म, अम्, n. a rope, cord.

शुष्मन्, आ, m. fire; a particular plant, = चि-
त्रक; (अ), n. light, lustre; strength, prowess.
शुष्मिण, अस्, m., N. of a king of the Śivis.

शुष्मिन्, ई, इणी, इ, powerful, strong; fiery, mettle-
some; (इणस्), m. pl., N. of a caste living in Kuśa-
dvīpa (corresponding to the Kṣatriyas).
—शुष्-
मिन्-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. most powerful, very
mighty.
शुष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming dry, drying up.

शुष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being dry or dried up,
languishing, thirsty.

शूशुजान शूशुजान, अस्, आ, अम् (according to
Sāy. = शोशुचान, दीप्यमान, Ṛg-veda X. 34, 6;
cf. शुशुचान, p. 1013), Ved. glowing, resplen-
dent.

शूशुवस् शूशुवस्, वान्, m. (fr. rt. श्वि), Ved.
one who has increased, increasing; large.

शूशुवान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. growing in size, in-
creasing in strength.

शूषणि, in Ṛg-veda X. 93, 1. probably fr. a
base शूषन्; regarded by some as a kind of Ved.
Inf. fr. rt. श्वि.

सुषुवाण, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has poured out
libations.

सुष्वयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (according to some
fr. a Nominal base सुष्वय, to which सुष्व-
यन्त, Ṛg-veda VII. 36, 6, may possibly also be
referred; but according to Sāy. derived fr. rt. अय्
with a reduplicated form of सु prefixed), Ved. pour-
ing out libations.

सुष्वाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. pouring out libations,
being poured forth, (Sāy. सुष्वाणेभिस् = सुन्वद्-
भिर् यजमानैः, Ṛg-veda IV. 29, 2; = सूय-
मान, IX. 101, 11; सुष्वाणः = यजमानेभ्यः
कामान् प्रेरयन्, as if fr. rt. 1. सू, Ṛg-veda IX.
6, 8.)

सुष्वि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. pouring out libations, offer-
ing sacrifices, (Sāy. सुष्विम् = सोमानाम् अभिषो-
तारम्, Ṛg-veda I. 61, 15; सुष्वये = सोमं
सुन्वते, Ṛg-veda IV. 25, 7.)
—सुष्वि-तर, अस्,
आ, अम्, Ved. making more libations, one who offers
frequent sacrifices.
सुष्वि सुष्वि. See under rt. 3. सु.
सुस्वान, अस्, आ, अम्, = सुष्वाण.

सुष्ठु, ind. (fr. सु + स्थु fr. rt. 1. स्था; accord-
ing to some ष्ठु = स्तु is merely an affix), well, excel-
lently, beautifully; much, very, exceedingly; truly.
—सुष्ठु-वह् or सुष्ठु-वाह्, -वाट्, ट्, ट्, Ved.
carrying well, bearing along rapidly (said of horses).
सुष्ठु सुष्ठु. See p. 1126, col. 3.
सुशीविका सुशीविका, f. a sort of yam.
सुषिलीका सुषिलीका, f., Ved. a kind of bird.

सुषुप्वस् सुषुप्वस्, सुषुप्सु. See under
rt. स्वप्.

सुषुप्वस्, आन्, उषी, अत्, one who has slept or
sleeps.
सुषुम्ण सु-षुम्ण. See p. 1125, col. 2.
सुषेण सु-षेण, &c. See p. 1125, col. 2.
सुस्ना सुस्ना. See सु-स्ना, p. 1125.

सुस्मूर्षमाण सुस्मूर्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr.
Desid. of rt. स्मृ), wishing or trying to recollect.

सुस्मूर्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, wishing to re-
member.

सूषणा, f. (perhaps fr. an old Desid. of rt. 3. सू,
without reduplication), ‘one desiring to bring forth,’
a mother.

सूष्यन्ती, f. (a woman) desiring to bring forth,
one who is parturient.

सुषुपाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. sleeping, (Sāy. =
सुप्त.)

सुषुप्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to sleep, sleepy,
drowsy.
